February 19, 2023 Geoffrey Siebengartner, Chairman American Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong 22/F, Hong Kong Diamond Exchange Building 8-10 Duddell Street, Central, Hong Kong Dear Mr. Siebengartner, I write to express my deep concern over your appearance in a recent promotional video created by Hong Kong’s pro-Beijing government.' The promotional video, which aims to attract foreign businesses, touts that Hong Kong has a “sound legal system.” By participating in this video, the American Chamber of Commerce in Hong Kong (AmCham Hong Kong) demonstrated support for and gave credibility to the video’s message. AmCham Hong Kong’s participation is particularly concerning because the video was released on February 2, four days before Hong Kong began a mass show trial of 47 pro-democracy activists.” As you know, in June 2020, China’s Standing Committee of the National People’s Congress passed the so-called Hong Kong National Security Law, which is a direct assault on the “one party, two systems” structure the Government of China pledged to uphold and the fundamental rights and freedoms of the people of Hong Kong. Since the passage of the National Security Law, Beijing has dismantled what remained of Hong Kong’s democratic institutions, jailed and disappeared dissidents, and violated its international obligations under the Sino-British Joint Declaration of 1984 and the Hong Kong Basic Law. In response to the enactment of this law, the U.S. Congress passed the Hong Kong Autonomy Act (PL116-149), which President Trump signed into law in July 2020. The Hong Kong Autonomy Act finds that the Government of China “has undertaken actions that have contravened the letter or intent of” its legal obligation to maintain Hong Kong’s “independent judicial power.” In the Hong Kong Policy Act Reports of 2021 and 2022, the U.S. Department of State found that the ' Quinn, Jimmy (@james_t_quinn). Hong Kong’s judicial independence was weakened in practice as local authorities consistently followed the Hong Kong National Security Law.

The US government has also found that China’s actions on Hong Kong increasingly deny the autonomy and freedom that China promised to the people of Hong Kong under the 1984 Sino- British Joint Declaration. For this reason, the Secretary of State announced that “Hong Kong no longer warrants treatment under U.S. law in the same manner as U.S. laws were applied to Hong Kong before July 1,
1997 (emphasis added).”?

In July 2022, the U.S. Congressional-Executive Commission on China found that “three years after the protests, the negative effects of political prosecution are evident. Important institutions that monitor government accountability, including the independent press and civil society organizations, have been rapidly dismantled under the broad and indiscriminate enforcement of the NSL and related laws. :.. Hong Kong government prosecutors are complicit in undermining the city’s once robust rule of law (emphasis added),” and thus urged President Biden to sanction Hong Kong prosecutors.*

In light of the overwhelming evidence that the National Security Law has undermined the fundamental rights and freedoms of the people of Hong Kong, it is deeply troubling that AmCham Hong Kong would participate in a video that falsely claims the opposite. According to media expert Mark Simon, the government of Hong Kong sees “the chamber and the U.S. government as one.” If this is the case, then this video may be interpreted as the U.S. Government quietly retracting its position on the status of rule of law in Hong Kong, and that would have profound implications.
For these reasons, I would like to offer AmCham Hong Kong an opportunity to clarify its own views on the matter. I therefore request that you respond to the following questions by Feb. 27, 2023:
Does AmCham Hong Kong believe that the Hong Kong National Security Law is consistent with the Sino-British Joint Declaration of 1984?
On AmCham Hong Kong’s bsite, “rule of law” is listed as one of its core values. a.

Please clarify what AmCham Hong means by the “rule of law.” b. Does AmCham Hong Kong believe that the National Security Law is consistent with “rule of law?” If so, please explain why. + Exec. Order.
